items.abstract: <jats:p>This study develops a comprehensive framework for designing sustainable supply chains in the era of digital transformation, addressing the increasing need to integrate advanced technological capabilities with sustainability objectives. A qualitative research approach was adopted, drawing on semi-structured interviews with industry professionals, supply chain managers, technology experts, and academic researchers. These insights were complemented by secondary data from industry reports and scholarly publications. The collected data were analyzed using thematic analysis to identify the core dimensions and enabling factors of sustainable supply chain design. The findings highlight three fundamental sustainability pillars environmental, social, and economic performance supported by critical enablers such as digital technologies, interorganizational collaboration, governance mechanisms, innovation, and human and organizational capabilities. The results further indicate that digital technologies, including artificial intelligence, the Internet of Things (IoT), blockchain, and big data analytics, significantly enhance supply chain visibility, optimize operational processes, support ethical and transparent practices, and enable proactive risk management. In addition, strong collaboration among supply chain partners and effective governance structures were identified as essential for successful implementation. However, challenges such as high implementation costs, skill shortages, and infrastructure limitations remain important barriers that require strategic planning and capability development. The study proposes a robust conceptual framework that integrates sustainability principles with digital transformation strategies. This framework provides practical guidance for organizations seeking to improve resilience, operational efficiency, and ethical performance within their supply chains, while also offering theoretical insights to support future research on sustainable supply chain design in digitally driven environments.</jats:p>
